gap:logistic_optimization.statement: Determine optimal L2 regularization strength, interaction feature benefit, and compression configuration for logistic regression on binary classification data using exact gradient descent implementation with specified hyperparameters.

hyp:l2_regularization_effect.statement: L2 regularization will improve generalization (lower Brier score) with an optimal lambda in the middle range [0.01, 0.1]; both lower and higher values will show worse performance due to underfitting or overfitting penalties.

claim:task1_results.statement: L2 regularization analysis across lambdas [0.0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0] shows optimal performance at lambda=0.1 with 5-fold CV Brier score of 0.207077, yielding 0.00890 improvement over baseline (lambda=0.0: 0.215977).

claim:task2_results.statement: Interaction features (x0*x1, x1*x2, x2*x3, x0*x3) significantly improve model performance with paired t-statistic of 3.912 across 5 folds, indicating raw mean Brier (0.2071) is substantially higher than interaction mean Brier (0.1814), confirming interaction_helps=true.

claim:task3_results.statement: Compression configuration sparsity20_bits4 achieves highest performance retention of 0.9992 (dense Brier: 0.1418, compressed Brier: 0.1419), significantly outperforming heavier sparsity levels (60% shows 0.9588 retention).
